current_rule: Model CIUS local annual rows as first-class source identity, keep CIUS/SRS/NIBRS source semantics explicit, treat CIUS as canonical annual observation rather than hidden SRS or fake monthly support, and stop allowing explosive two-point local trend projection.
evidence_summary: Repo review found CIUS promoted as srs_return_a_annual with provenance flags, which forced downstream source-selection and estimator code to reason about 'secret CIUS SRS rows'. Local observations, tracker context, UCR book guidance, and official FBI/BJS transition materials support a cleaner doctrine: CIUS is the canonical FBI-published local annual row when present; otherwise SRS and NIBRS arbitrate as distinct sources by quality. Follow-up review also found CIUS rows being mislabeled as `full_monthly` in the reporting-regime layer even though CIUS only proves annual published completeness, and found the municipal estimator using a blunter regime-only observed rule than the jurisdiction estimator. The same review found the panel estimator allowing explosive two-point log-linear projection, which produced absurd 2020-2021 local estimates.
next_action: promote_cius_publication_annual_as_first_class_source_treat_it_as_annual_observed_not_monthly_and_raise_local_trend_projection_guardrails_to_3_usable_years_with_1_year_gap

current_rule: Let any numeric non-protected non-count-like column flow into the model path as long as its dtype is numeric.
evidence_summary: The live BG frame showed several dead or near-dead features surviving selection solely because they were numeric: `road_median_length_km` was constant, `hh_family_other_share` was constant, and `other_road_length_km` had only about `0.2%` non-null coverage with effectively zero non-zero support. Leaving those columns in the shared feature stack adds noise and obscures which families are genuinely informative. The safer generic rule is to require a minimum information floor before a numeric column is eligible for the model path.
next_action: Keep numeric feature selection generic but enforce minimum-information gates: require at least `1%` non-null coverage, at least `2` unique non-null values, and at least `0.1%` non-zero support before a column reaches the model-selection stage.

current_rule: Use NIBRS-derived counts as a drop-in universal replacement for SRS wherever NIBRS exists.
evidence_summary: Local QA artifacts comparing Kaplan SRS-style agency-year counts to our NIBRS-derived hierarchy-collapse counts show that the two are not uniformly interchangeable even on overlapping fully reported agencies. In the 2024 12-month overlap bucket, aggregate NIBRS/SRS ratios are close for robbery (~0.986) and larceny (~1.002), but materially lower for rape (~0.755) and aggravated assault (~0.814). The new state-level audit at artifacts/qa/srs_nibrs_exploration/srs_vs_nibrs_state_ratios_2024_12m.csv shows that this is not just one national tail: the same pattern recurs across large states like TX, MI, CA, VA, GA, and NC.
next_action: Keep NIBRS in V2 as explicit parallel or fallback annual support; if broader substitution is ever considered, require offense-aware validation and documented reconciliation rather than treating NIBRS-derived counts as automatically equivalent to the traditional SRS-style series.

current_rule: Treat 2024 NIBRS-backed rows as if they imply one seamless pre-2021-to-2024 NIBRS/SRS reconciliation framework already exists in V2.
evidence_summary: Official BJS/FBI materials distinguish three regimes: pre-2021 traditional estimates already combined SRS with NIBRS submissions converted down to SRS-style counts; 2021 used a distinct NIBRS-only estimation framework because coverage collapsed; 2022-2024 restored hybrid traditional estimates alongside separate NIBRS-only estimates. Local V2 code currently uses NIBRS mainly as annual fallback/parallel support, not as a full historical reconciliation layer.
next_action: Keep the current 2024 NIBRS annual-support lane explicit and narrow; if we later extend historical continuity logic, implement it as a deliberate reconciliation workstream rather than assuming the current fallback machinery already does that job.

current_rule: Treat the Kaplan/OpenICPSR SRS annual field `number_of_months_reported` as a literal count of reported months and propagate it through production as canonical `months_reported`.
evidence_summary: The exact raw annual source used by V2 carries both `number_of_months_reported` and `last_month_reported`, and the live 2024 file aligns them exactly as a last-month code (`12 -> december`, `11 -> november`, ..., `0 -> no months reported`). Kaplan's openICPSR release notes explicitly say `last_month_reported` is how the FBI defines `number_of_months_reported` and that the old variable name is misleading. V2 then amplified that ambiguity by renaming raw `number_of_months_reported` to plain `months_reported` in production builders and using it as if it were a true completeness denominator. The safe canonical quantity is the true non-missing SRS month count derived from the monthly `month_missing` mask; annual `number_of_months_missing` is only a fallback when monthly detail is unavailable. After patching observations, reporting regimes, controls, reference helpers, and the exploratory QA script, fallback-SRS rows match raw monthly non-missing month counts exactly once the audit uses the same production keying rule, `COALESCE(NULLIF(ori9,''), ori || '00')`. The earlier apparent mismatch tail was an audit join bug, not a residual source inconsistency problem.
next_action: Keep the corrected SRS semantics locked in the spec/tracker, treat CIUS-backed summary rows as intentionally separate complete-reporter semantics, and audit raw SRS monthly consistency only with the same ORI coalescing rule used in production.

current_rule: Fix the production-promotion gap where reviewed municipal-target drop decisions were suppressing review queues but not actually changing the live reference/control build.
evidence_summary: The architecture audit found a real divergence between review state and production state: active reviewed drop conclusions for Brookhaven town, Islip town, Silver Spring CDP, Owings Mills CDP, College Park MD, Babylon town, and Huntington town NY existed in configs/service_structure_notes.csv and removed those cases from the municipal review queue, but production never consumed that free-text note file. Those invalid rows therefore stayed alive in jurisdiction_master, jurisdiction_controls_2024, and the 2024 non-observed tail. The fix was to promote the reviewed drop cases into the canonical production override surface, configs/municipal_geometry_overrides.csv, as explicit exclude decisions and then rebuild the full downstream chain through reference, observations, reporting regimes, municipal estimates, controls, geometry, and outputs.
next_action: Keep service_structure_notes as review/log material only; every reviewed drop or remap that should affect production must be promoted into a canonical override surface rather than assumed to flow through automatically.

current_rule: Fix the live output-build failure in src/crimerisk/allocation.py caused by non-boolean overlap grouping masks reaching np.select.
evidence_summary: After the rebuilt reference/control chain, python main.py build-outputs failed in _build_overlap_group_targets because one of the overlap-treatment masks had nullable/object boolean dtype and numpy.select rejected it. The logic itself was still correct; the bug was mask typing. The fix was to coerce every overlap group condition mask to an explicit boolean ndarray before passing the condlist into np.select, after which build-outputs completed and rewrote the live ags_core outputs.
next_action: When pandas nullable/string-derived masks feed numpy branching in production code, coerce them explicitly to plain boolean ndarrays instead of assuming numpy will accept extension-dtype masks.

current_rule: Apply local-resolution override decisions consistently to nonlocal final routing, not just full_local rows.
evidence_summary: The architecture audit found that configs/local_resolution_overrides.csv only changed full_local rows. That meant reviewed municipal reroutes for nonlocal agencies could exist in tracker doctrine without ever changing production routing. The concrete live failure was FL0160000 Jacksonville Sheriff's Office still feeding 12:state_nonmunicipal_remainder even though the reviewed Jacksonville doctrine required it to anchor Jacksonville city. The fix was to teach src/crimerisk/jurisdiction_reference.py to apply municipal_place, municipal_cousub, reclassify_nonmunicipal, and reclassify_overlap overrides to full_nonlocal rows and then promote FL0160000 into configs/local_resolution_overrides.csv as a municipal_place override for Jacksonville city.
next_action: Keep configs/local_resolution_overrides.csv as the canonical reroute surface for both local and nonlocal rows; do not assume reviewed doctrine changes production unless the nonlocal path consumes the same override contract.

current_rule: Handle state official annual publication rows as a first-class source lane instead of forcing Florida official data through SRS semantics or ORI-by-ORI hacks.
evidence_summary: Implemented the first live state-official publication lane as source = state_publication_annual. Added src/crimerisk/state_publications.py to ingest quarter-complete 2024 FDLE annual/YTD offense totals, map them to AGS offenses, and promote them into agency observations with raw_data_source = fdle_fibrs_offense_detail_ytd. Then wired state_publication_annual through source_provenance, observations, reporting_regimes, source_selection, municipal_estimator, jurisdiction_estimator, and controls so official state-publication rows are treated as explicit annual observed support rather than disguised SRS behavior. Verified intermediate rebuilt outputs show Jacksonville city and Fort Lauderdale city using preferred_source = state_publication_annual with reported_regime_usable support while Miami Beach correctly remains outside the lane because the reviewed FDLE annual surface is still only three quarters complete there.
next_action: Treat state-official publication lanes as explicit source identities with state-specific completeness rules; use Florida as the first implementation and keep Mississippi as the next state-official source lane rather than burying this work inside generic SRS/NIBRS arbitration.

current_rule: Limit official-publication matcher aliases to canonical ORI-backed agencies so synthetic roster noise cannot block valid state-publication matches.
evidence_summary: The Florida official-publication matcher initially missed clean cities like Fort Lauderdale because synthetic Broward-style NIBRS roster rows with ...X ORIs were allowed to generate publication aliases, making official names like Fort Lauderdale Police Department ambiguous even though the real municipal ORI was present. The fix in src/crimerisk/state_publications.py was to build publication aliases only from canonical ORI-backed agencies with ori7 present and from exclusive jurisdiction aliases tied to those canonical agencies. After that change the live FDLE lane increased to 959 offense rows across 137 ORIs and correctly matched Jacksonville, Fort Lauderdale, Fort Myers, and Palm Beach Gardens without introducing Florida-specific hardcoded exceptions.
next_action: For state-official publication matching, use canonical agency identities plus reviewed jurisdiction aliases, not every synthetic or roster-derived agency stub that happens to share a city name.

current_rule: Use the municipal target-year estimator as the single source-of-truth for municipal current-year preferred source and observed-vs-fill status once it has resolved a case.
evidence_summary: The Florida state-publication lane exposed a second architecture contradiction after reporting and municipal estimates were already correct: municipal_estimates_2024.parquet had Jacksonville city and Fort Lauderdale city on preferred_source = state_publication_annual with reported_regime_usable support, but jurisdiction_estimator.py and the downstream controls build were still reconstructing a competing preferred-source story directly from agency-preferred observations and only using municipal estimates as a zero-count fill patch. That collapsed both cities back to observed_nibrs_rollup in the final 2024 controls even though the municipal estimator had already resolved the target-year municipal truth. The fix was to promote target-year municipal preferred-source truth, reported_count_preferred, dominant_reporting_regime, and estimated_count into the jurisdiction-year estimator for municipal rows so the panel, controls, and municipal estimator now share one current-year municipal source decision.
next_action: Keep one target-year municipal truth path: once municipal_estimates resolves a municipal row for the release year, downstream jurisdiction-year estimation and controls must consume that resolution instead of reconstructing a parallel municipal preferred-source stack from agency-level observations.

current_rule: Keep the shared agency-preferred source path aligned with the live source ontology so new first-class sources cannot be silently dropped before arbitration.
evidence_summary: After the Florida state-publication lane landed, the architecture audit found that src/crimerisk/source_selection.py still filtered the agency observation table down to CIUS / SRS / NIBRS before it built the shared agency-preferred source panel. That meant state_publication_annual rows were present in observations, reporting regimes, municipal_estimator, jurisdiction_estimator, and controls, but were still being silently excluded from build_agency_preferred_observations. The fix was to include state_publication_annual in that filter and then centralize the preferred-source initializer and preferred-value routing in shared helpers inside src/crimerisk/source_provenance.py so source_selection.py, municipal_estimator.py, and controls.py no longer carry slightly different hand-rolled precedence logic.
next_action: When a new first-class source lane is added, audit every shared arbitration path against the source ontology and prefer one shared precedence helper over parallel local rewrites.

current_rule: Carry preferred-source metadata through the jurisdiction-year panel instead of recomputing pieces of it later in controls.
evidence_summary: The same source-policy audit found that after the panel merge, controls.py still rebuilt pieces of preferred-source metadata locally from partial maps or default source-label logic. The concrete cleanup in this tranche was to (1) replace a local hardcoded preferred_source_origin fallback with source_origin_from_parts(...), (2) promote preferred_conversion_status into jurisdiction_year_estimates so controls.py can consume panel metadata instead of reconstructing it from the bare source label, (3) fix preferred_state_exception_flag so state_publication_annual rows no longer advertise false negative metadata, and (4) remove ontology drift by making STATE_PUBLICATION_SOURCE canonical in source_provenance.py and importing it from there rather than redefining or re-exporting it through producer modules.
next_action: Keep provenance and source-policy metadata first-class in the panel artifacts; avoid downstream local reconstructions, lying summary flags, and duplicate source constants that can drift out of sync.

current_rule: Apply the same true-partial annualization doctrine in the municipal target-year estimator that the jurisdiction-year estimator already uses.
evidence_summary: The architecture audit found that src/crimerisk/municipal_estimator.py never implemented a target-year true-partial branch. Municipal rows with preferred_source = srs_return_a_annual, dominant_reporting_regime = true_partial, positive counts, and sub-12 month coverage were falling straight through to trend_log_linear or other history fills even though the main jurisdiction estimator already treated the same condition as true_partial_month_ratio. The fix was to carry mean_months_reported_preferred through the municipal regime-aware panel and then annualize municipal target-year summary rows with 0 < months < 12 via true_partial_month_ratio before any trend or historical fallback logic runs.
next_action: Keep partial-year annualization doctrine consistent across municipal and jurisdiction estimators; if a target-year summary row is explicitly true_partial with positive counts and bounded month coverage, annualize it before invoking trend or historical fallback.

current_rule: Make the controls build surface explicit about its dependence on the municipal-estimates artifact so estimator fixes cannot stay hidden behind stale cached parquets.
evidence_summary: While validating the municipal true-partial fix, the live controls artifact kept showing stale trend_log_linear rows for Doral and St. Augustine even after the municipal estimator code was corrected. The issue was not the estimator logic anymore; build-controls was reusing the previously materialized state/modeling/municipal_estimates_2024.parquet by default. Rebuilding municipal estimates first fixed the downstream controls output. The CLI is now being hardened so build-controls exposes an explicit force-municipal-estimates-rebuild path instead of hiding that dependency behind cached state.
next_action: Do not let downstream builds silently depend on stale intermediate modeling artifacts; either rebuild the dependency explicitly or expose a clear force-rebuild option at the CLI boundary.

current_rule: Implement Mississippi Crime Insight / TOPS as the second live state-official publication lane on the same first-class source path as Florida.
evidence_summary: Added a Mississippi provider to src/crimerisk/state_publications.py and wired it through the existing state_publication_annual path rather than creating a Mississippi-specific sidecar. The provider now pulls official TOPS report 105 and 115 CSV exports for canonical Mississippi ORIs, caches the raw responses under data/MS-TOPS-2024/raw, writes the parsed canonical extract to data/MS-TOPS-2024/parsed/ms_tops_2024_offense_extract.csv, validates each returned jurisdiction header against the queried ORI's canonical alias set so invalid-member requests cannot silently fall back to statewide Mississippi totals, and uses retry plus a final sequential pass so the state site remains stable under full-cache builds. After rebuilding observations, reporting regimes, and controls, the live Mississippi lane contributes 542 official offense rows across 111 ORIs; all 542 reporting-regime rows classify as annual_only_but_usable; Mississippi 2024 agency preferred-source arbitration now includes 542 state_publication_annual rows; and 8 of the packet's 40 effective-NIBRS zero-observation backfill candidates now carry direct official Mississippi support.
next_action: Treat Mississippi as a live state-official source lane with the same explicit source ontology as Florida. The remaining Mississippi problem is now source selection and residual official-coverage tail review, not extractor availability.

current_rule: Normalize Mississippi TOPS status-prefixed jurisdiction labels after text standardization and rebuild the parsed extract from raw cache on every call so provider fixes cannot hide behind stale parsed artifacts.
evidence_summary: The first Mississippi TOPS pass exposed a second provider-level issue. After _std_text() stripped punctuation, status-prefixed labels like 'Recert - Walls Police Department' and 'Not Reporting Certified - Bolivar County Sheriff's Office' were arriving as 'RECERT WALLS ...' and 'NOT REPORTING CERTIFIED ...', so the original prefix stripper no longer matched and those clean official rows stayed outside the parsed extract. At the same time, ensure_ms_tops_annual_extract(...) was short-circuiting on an existing parsed CSV, which meant matcher changes could remain hidden behind stale parsed state even though the raw TOPS cache was already present. The fix was to make the status-prefix normalizer accept both hyphenated and space-only forms after text standardization, keep agency_name_raw in the canonical alias frame, and always rebuild the parsed Mississippi extract from the raw cache on each call. After rebuilding observations, reporting regimes, and controls, Mississippi state-publication support increased from 542 rows across 111 ORIs to 624 rows across 133 ORIs, and direct effective-NIBRS backfill coverage increased from 8 to 12 candidate agencies.
next_action: When a provider relies on cached raw extracts, keep the parsed layer derivable and refreshable from raw cache by default so matcher/normalization fixes immediately propagate. Also normalize status-bearing official labels after whatever text-standardization step actually runs first, not against the prettier pre-normalized string you wish you had.

current_rule: Reclassify the residual Mississippi packet tail after live ingestion so stale packet assumptions do not keep masquerading as active 2024 production work.
evidence_summary: After the live Mississippi TOPS lane landed, the packet still described the remaining tail as 28 uncovered effective-NIBRS backfill candidates plus one live missing-master omission. A direct post-ingestion audit against the cached raw report_105/report_115 exports and fresh Louin probes showed a different reality. Of the packet's 40 backfill candidates, 12 already carry live state_publication_annual support, 26 have no offense-bearing 2024 target rows in the raw TOPS surfaces at all, 1 has only non-target 2024 property support (Sandersville PD), and only 1 still looks like a real recoverable alias tail (Southwest Mississippi Community College, burglary=5). Direct 2026-03-26 TOPS probes for Louin (MS0310300) returned no offense-bearing 2024 rows, so that note should no longer be treated as a live production omission until an official offense-bearing row actually appears.
next_action: Once a state-official lane is live, re-audit any pre-ingestion packet queues against the actual landed raw and parsed surfaces. Do not keep treating packet-era candidate counts or missing-master notes as active production work if the live official source does not currently yield offense-bearing target-year rows.

current_rule: Carry quarter-aware state-publication rows through reporting, municipal estimation, panel estimation, and controls as true_partial support instead of degrading them back to zero-only SRS/fill behavior.
evidence_summary: Florida exposed a second-order wiring problem after the first state-publication lane landed. The raw observation and reporting layers were already correct for quarter-limited FDLE rows, but later stages still had three contradictions: reporting_regimes.py was clobbering all state_publication_annual preferred rows back to annual_only_but_usable, municipal_estimator.py annualized only SUMMARY_SOURCE true_partial rows, and the municipal target-year override path in jurisdiction_estimator.py force-stamped state-publication month coverage to 12. After fixing those paths and rebuilding, quarter-limited FDLE rows such as Miami Beach, Cape Coral, Davie, Fort Pierce, and Port St. Lucie now land cleanly as preferred_source = state_publication_annual, dominant_reporting_regime = true_partial, and estimate_source = true_partial_month_ratio in the final panel/control layer rather than degrading to zero-only SRS plus hist_median or peer fill.
next_action: If a state-official annual publication lane carries bounded target-year coverage rather than a full-year row, treat it end to end as true_partial support. Do not silently collapse that row into complete annual support or back into zero-only fallback behavior later in the estimator stack.

current_rule: Keep force-rebuild CLI paths behaviorally coherent across all outputs they write; one command must not emit sibling artifacts built from different dependency states.
evidence_summary: A follow-through audit on Florida partial-official handling exposed two hidden wrapper bugs. First, write_v2_controls(...) accepted --force-municipal-estimates-rebuild but only passed that dependency refresh to the control build, not to the jurisdiction_year_estimates artifact written by the same command, so build-controls could emit internally contradictory outputs from one invocation. Second, once the force flag was threaded through, the corresponding path in jurisdiction_estimator.py was revealed as dead code: it tried to instantiate MunicipalEstimatorConfig(year=...) even though the config had no year field. The fix was to (1) propagate force_municipal_estimates_rebuild through write_v2_controls into the jurisdiction-year estimator build, (2) add force_reporting_regimes_rebuild to MunicipalEstimatorConfig so the municipal rebuild path is internally coherent, and (3) replace the invalid year=... call with year_start = year_end = target_year = release year.
next_action: Treat CLI force flags as contract surfaces, not convenience hints. If a command writes multiple sibling artifacts, every output must be built from the same refreshed dependency state, and the forced path must actually execute rather than hiding dead code behind the cached default path.

current_rule: Expose reporting-regime rebuild control on the municipal and controls build commands so those wrappers cannot silently rely on a stale modeling artifact after source or regime logic changes.
evidence_summary: The follow-through audit showed that ControlBuildConfig and MunicipalEstimatorConfig both already carried force_reporting_regimes_rebuild, but the user-facing build-controls and build-municipal-estimates commands did not expose that flag at all. In practice that meant reporting-regime logic could change while the main downstream build wrappers still reused the cached agency_year_reporting_regimes.parquet artifact unless the operator already knew to run build-reporting-regimes manually first. The fix was to add --force-reporting-regimes-rebuild to both CLI commands and pass it through the wrappers into the corresponding configs.
next_action: If a downstream build genuinely depends on a cached modeling artifact, expose the rebuild control at the command boundary. A code-only force flag is not a real build contract and will eventually produce stale, contradictory outputs.

current_rule: Expose geometry cache invalidation at the CLI boundary so build-geometry can rebuild stale per-state block assignments instead of always silently reusing cached shards.
evidence_summary: The same wrapper audit that found stale reporting-regime controls exposed an analogous geometry problem. build_block_crosswalk(...) already accepted force_rebuild and cached per-state block assignments under state/geometry/blocks_by_state, but write_v2_geometry(...) and the user-facing build-geometry command never surfaced or passed that control. As a result, changing reference/geometry logic could still leave build-geometry reusing stale state shards while appearing to rebuild the top-level crosswalk outputs. The fix was to thread force_rebuild through write_v2_geometry(...) and expose --force-rebuild on build-geometry.
next_action: If a command writes artifacts from cached per-state shards, surface the shard rebuild control at the CLI boundary. Otherwise a nominal rebuild can still be behaviorally stale.

current_rule: Promote the city incident share surface into the canonical src/ CLI build path and reject stale cache reuse when the enabled city set changes.
evidence_summary: The architecture audit found that build-outputs consumed state/modeling/city_incident_share_surface.parquet as a production input even though that artifact was only produced by a side script under scripts/review/city. Worse, the allocator treated a missing artifact as an empty frame, and the cached artifact remained reusable even after the packet/config gates moved on to a different enabled city set. The fix was to add src/crimerisk/city_shares.py as the canonical builder, expose build-city-incident-shares in the main CLI, add --force-city-incident-share-rebuild to build-outputs, and validate the cached artifact against the currently enabled city set before reusing it. Once that cache validation was made explicit, the repo surfaced a real blocker instead of hiding it: san_francisco is currently enabled by packet/config truth but does not yet have canonical builder support.
next_action: Do not let review-side scripts remain the only producers of live production inputs. Promote those builders into the canonical src/CLI path, and never treat a cached artifact as valid if the current enablement gates no longer match the content it was built for.

current_rule: Make city incident share rebuild controls explicit about whether they rebuild only the derived artifact or also refresh the underlying raw city-source cache.
evidence_summary: The next architecture-audit pass found that even after city_shares.py became canonical, force-rebuilding the city incident share artifact still reused whatever raw Socrata/cache snapshot happened to be on disk. That made the build contract ambiguous: a nominal rebuild could still be behaviorally stale if the upstream city feed had changed. The fix was to add an explicit raw-source refresh contract through build-city-incident-shares --force-source-refresh and build-outputs --force-city-incident-source-refresh, thread that control through the canonical city-share builders, and treat source refresh as a first-class rebuild choice rather than an implicit side effect.
next_action: When production code depends on cached third-party city-source pulls, separate artifact rebuild from source refresh explicitly. Do not let a nominal rebuild silently reuse a stale raw-source snapshot.

current_rule: Keep the San Francisco incident feed at raw row granularity until the packet-reviewed incident_number x offense hardening step, rather than collapsing rows earlier on incident_id.
evidence_summary: The first canonical San Francisco builder pass materially undercounted robbery aggravated_assault burglary larceny and motor_vehicle_theft even though the packet-local hardening artifacts and the raw DataSF feed already supported the reviewed five-offense path. The root cause was architectural rather than substantive: _load_san_francisco_raw_snapshot(...) was deduping the raw feed on incident_id before offense mapping. In the live DataSF contract, multiple rows can share one incident_id while carrying different offense-bearing or courtesy/update semantics. That early collapse could replace the offense-bearing row with a courtesy report or lower-severity row before mapping ever happened. The fix was to stop deduping on incident_id, preserve the raw feed through mapping, and then apply the packet-style incident_number x v2_offense dedupe contract later in the canonical builder. After rebuild, the canonical San Francisco counts returned to the reviewed offense-selective boundary and the live ags_core outputs were rewritten against that surface.
next_action: Do not collapse multi-row city incident feeds before the offense-harmonization contract has been applied. Preserve raw rows until the reviewed dedupe grain is known, and encode that dedupe grain explicitly in the canonical builder instead of inferring a simpler early unique key.

current_rule: Promote Austin into the live canonical city-share surface for the bounded exact four-offense path once packet truth, central gating, and the canonical builder all agree.
evidence_summary: A follow-through audit on city/local-source promotion found that Austin was stuck in a contradictory state. The packet already said the exact offense-selective path was ready for robbery burglary larceny and motor_vehicle_theft, and the canonical Austin builder already reproduced that boundary against the official published 2024 counts within a few percent, but central gating still kept Austin out of the live city-share surface through stale packet-status wording and notes that still described promotion as future work. The fix was to normalize the Austin packet status to production_ready = yes with offense_selective city-share integration status, update the central source/priority notes to match the live doctrine, rebuild the canonical city-share artifact, and rebuild the live ags_core outputs. Aggravated assault remains intentionally blocked because the empirical refresh candidate still conflicts with APD's published offense-code lookup.
next_action: When a city packet, central gating, and the canonical builder already agree on a bounded offense-selective production path, promote it cleanly instead of leaving stale status text to keep the city packet-only. Keep the blocked offenses explicit rather than delaying the promotable slice for the whole city.

current_rule: Make build-outputs a coherent top-level wrapper for its direct upstream artifacts instead of assuming hidden manual pre-steps.
evidence_summary: The next architecture-audit pass found that build-outputs still looked like a canonical top-level command while silently assuming jurisdiction_controls_2024.parquet, state_control_comparison.parquet, jurisdiction_year_estimates.parquet, block_group_to_jurisdiction_crosswalk.parquet, and bg_prior_long_2024.parquet were already current. That made one command capable of writing fresh final outputs from stale controls, stale geometry, or a stale modeled-surface cache. The fix was to add explicit rebuild controls to AllocationBuildConfig and the CLI/script wrappers so build-outputs can now rebuild controls, reporting regimes, municipal estimates, geometry, and the cached BG prior before allocation when requested or when required artifacts are missing.
next_action: If a top-level command writes final release artifacts, its direct upstream rebuild contract must be explicit at the command boundary. Do not rely on operators to know hidden sibling-artifact pre-steps.

current_rule: Invalidate the cached BG prior when the block-group geometry crosswalk changes.
evidence_summary: The same wrapper audit exposed a real stale-cache bug in src/crimerisk/allocation.py: bg_prior_long_2024.parquet depended operationally on the block_group_to_jurisdiction_crosswalk used inside build_bg_feature_frame and build_model_surface, but the cache dependency check only watched controls and selected covariate inputs. That meant geometry changes could leave the modeled-surface cache behaviorally stale even after geometry rebuilds succeeded. The fix was to add the block-group geometry crosswalk to the BG-prior dependency set and to force a BG-prior rebuild automatically when build-outputs is asked to rebuild geometry.
next_action: Cache invalidation for modeled surfaces must include every artifact that changes the effective training/application frame, not just the obvious covariate files.

current_rule: Centralize the shared NIBRS-over-summary preference rule so agency selection and controls cannot drift apart on the same arbitration question.
evidence_summary: A follow-through source-policy audit found that src/crimerisk/source_selection.py and src/crimerisk/controls.py still carried near-duplicate boolean logic for when NIBRS should outrank summary/SRS after CIUS and state-publication precedence were applied. The rules were intended to be the same, but they had already diverged once during the broader source reset, which is exactly the kind of hidden contradiction that makes the pipeline hard to reason about. The fix was to move that shared boolean into build_prefer_nibrs_mask(...) inside src/crimerisk/source_provenance.py and make both call sites use the same helper. Municipal-estimator simplification remains a separate follow-through audit item.
next_action: When two live layers answer the same source-arbitration question, keep the rule in one shared helper instead of duplicating the boolean expression and hoping they stay synchronized.

current_rule: Use the same shared NIBRS-over-summary preference helper in the municipal estimator that the agency selector and control layer already use.
evidence_summary: A follow-through architecture audit found one remaining live source-arbitration fork: src/crimerisk/municipal_estimator.py still preferred NIBRS only when no SRS existed or the dominant regime had already explicitly chosen NIBRS, while src/crimerisk/source_selection.py and src/crimerisk/controls.py were already using the shared build_prefer_nibrs_mask(...) helper. That left municipal target-year source choice behaviorally different from the rest of the pipeline. The fix was to route the municipal estimator through the same helper with its available regime and month-coverage signals. On the live regime-aware municipal panel this changes 606 municipal jurisdiction-year-offense rows, including large downward Florida 2020 larceny/burglary cleanups where implausible or weaker SRS rows had been winning and upward recoveries such as Lakewood CO 2019 and Athens CCD GA 2019 where NIBRS had stronger support than the old municipal shortcut recognized.
next_action: Keep source arbitration centralized. If municipal estimation, agency selection, and controls answer the same SRS-vs-NIBRS question, they must share one helper rather than parallel local rewrites.

current_rule: Keep the top-level configs surface honest about which CSVs are production-wired, which are review-only, and which are dormant templates.
evidence_summary: A repo-surface audit found that several CSVs under configs/ looked equally canonical from the root even though only a subset are actually read by live src production code. In particular, service_structure_notes.csv, feature_source_inventory.csv, and model_diagnostic_review.csv are review/program-support surfaces rather than production inputs, while municipal_target_overrides.csv and jurisdiction_overrides.csv are currently dormant templates not wired into live src production. README now distinguishes those classes explicitly instead of implying that every top-level CSV is a live override surface.
next_action: Do not present review notes or dormant templates as if they were active production config. Either wire a config into live src code, archive it, or label it clearly as review/support or dormant.

current_rule: Keep municipal_target_overrides.csv and jurisdiction_overrides.csv intentionally dormant until the repo has an explicit contract and consuming src build path for them.
evidence_summary: The follow-through architecture audit confirmed that these files are empty or under-specified templates rather than partially implemented production surfaces. No live src production code reads them, and wiring them now would create exactly the kind of half-finished override path that has previously made the repo hard to reason about. The tracker and README now state that they remain intentionally unwired at the current stage.
next_action: Leave the templates on disk for future deliberate design work, but do not wire them, populate them, or treat them as active production configs until their contract and rebuild implications are explicit.

current_rule: Treat packet_status.csv and packet_offense_status.csv as durable, versioned production-gating inputs wherever the live build depends on them.
evidence_summary: A follow-through architecture audit on the city-share lane found a real hidden contradiction. Central config and canonical builder support still treated New York, Chicago, and Seattle as active first-wave city paths, but the repo had already switched the live gate to packet-local status files and those packet_status.csv files were still stale scaffold placeholders. Because those packet files lived under ignored state/, the effective production gate had drifted without normal version-control visibility and the live city_incident_share_surface.parquet had silently shrunk to only Austin and San Francisco. The fix was twofold: normalize the stale packet status files to match reviewed packet truth, and force-track all packet_status.csv and packet_offense_status.csv files so future production-gating changes cannot hide in ignored local state.
next_action: When packet-local status files are behavior-bearing inputs to the live build, they must be treated as durable versioned state rather than ignored scratch review output. Keep summary artifacts regenerable, but track the packet gate files themselves.

current_rule: Treat any packet-side file read directly by live src builders as durable repo state, and invalidate city-share cache reuse when those packet inputs change.
evidence_summary: A deeper follow-through audit found that the canonical San Francisco city-share builder in src/crimerisk/city_shares.py and src/crimerisk/city_incidents.py still depended on packet-side offense_crosswalk.csv and published_reference_extract.csv under state/review/packets/city/san_francisco, but those files were not versioned and the city-share cache contract only checked enabled city keys. That meant the live canonical build still depended on invisible local state, and offense-gate or packet-input changes could leave city_incident_share_surface.parquet behaviorally stale even when the city set itself did not change. The fix was to treat the San Francisco packet-side builder inputs as durable repo state, declare them as explicit required_paths in the canonical city builder surface, extend QA to surface enabled_missing_required_inputs, and make city-share cache reuse invalidate on packet/config input mtimes instead of only the enabled city set.
next_action: If live src production code reads a packet-side file, that file is not scratch review output anymore. Version it, declare it in the build contract, and make cache reuse sensitive to it so packet-input drift cannot hide behind artifact reuse.

current_rule: Canonicalize Pennsylvania municipal place rows to municipal cousub when an exact TIGER borough-equivalent cousub exists with the same standardized label and local code, even if no paired cousub row already exists in full_local.
evidence_summary: A follow-through audit on the hidden Pennsylvania borough tail found that Doylestown borough and Nazareth borough still survived in the live 2024 controls as municipal place rows with no direct BG support. The underlying code bug was in _canonicalize_pa_equivalent_place_cousub_rows(...): it only remapped a Pennsylvania municipal place row when both the place and the matching cousub were already present inside full_local. For borough police rows like PA0090400 and PA0480700, the exact TIGER cousub existed and the geometry layer already carried those cousub IDs, but no paired local cousub row had been generated upstream, so the canonicalizer never ran. The fix was to let the Pennsylvania canonicalizer fall back to exact TIGER cousub lookup when standardized label and local code match. After rebuilding reference layers, PA0090400 now resolves to 42:municipal:cousub:4201719784 and PA0480700 now resolves to 42:municipal:cousub:4209552808.
next_action: Do not require an already-materialized paired local cousub row to recognize Pennsylvania borough-equivalent geography. If the exact TIGER cousub match is unambiguous and carries the same local code, canonicalize to municipal_cousub directly.

current_rule: Keep first-class build stages symmetrical across the CLI and thin scripts/build wrappers unless there is a deliberate reason not to.
evidence_summary: A repo-surface audit found that build-city-incident-shares had been promoted to a first-class CLI command and documented as part of the active build surface, but unlike the other active build stages it still lacked a matching thin scripts/build wrapper. That asymmetry was small, but it made the repo surface harder to scan and implied a special-case stage even though the underlying city-share path was already canonical. The fix was to add scripts/build/city_incident_shares.py against the live CityIncidentShareBuildConfig and write_v2_city_incident_shares(...) API and update README accordingly.
next_action: When a stage is first-class in the active build surface, either expose a matching thin wrapper or document clearly why it is intentionally CLI-only. Avoid accidental one-off build stages that exist only because no one finished the wrapper.

current_rule: Keep supplemental municipal block-group support inside the canonical geometry artifact with explicit allocation shares, and do not let outputs inject a hidden fallback crosswalk at allocation time.
evidence_summary: A post-reference rebuild audit found that the old live output path could still manufacture supplemental municipal BG support inside allocation.py through _build_missing_municipal_bg_crosswalk(...). That meant the canonical geometry artifact could stay incomplete while outputs still reconciled, which concealed real reference/geometry problems and made the build harder to reason about. The fix was to move supplemental municipal BG support into build-geometry, write explicit allocation_share rows into state/geometry/block_group_to_jurisdiction_crosswalk.parquet, and make build-outputs consume that canonical geometry artifact directly. After rebuild, QA shows missing_municipal_support_count_raw = 0, missing_municipal_support_count = 0, missing_municipal_support_fallback_rows = 0, and output-control differences only at floating-point noise.
next_action: If small-area support is needed for live outputs, materialize it in the geometry artifact itself. Do not hide geometry repairs inside allocation-time fallback code.

current_rule: Treat city incident overlays as within-jurisdiction share refinements rather than as silent jurisdiction-total replacements.
evidence_summary: A broader audit and user-facing conceptual check confirmed that the city-share surface solves a different problem from the jurisdiction-control layer. Local incident data such as NYC or Chicago geocoded incidents can materially improve where crime is placed inside the city, but they do not by themselves redefine the municipal control unit or replace the city's jurisdiction total. The live allocation path already behaves this way: city shares override within-jurisdiction BG shares while the municipal control total remains fixed upstream. The tracker and spec were updated to make that contract explicit so city-source promotion does not get mistaken for jurisdiction-layer rebuilding.
next_action: Keep city-share work scoped to within-jurisdiction allocation realism unless the upstream jurisdiction layer is intentionally rebuilt.

current_rule: Invalidate the cached BG prior on the real model-surface code paths rather than on nonexistent placeholder paths under src/.
evidence_summary: An architecture-audit pass found that src/crimerisk/allocation.py was deciding whether bg_prior_long_2024.parquet was current by checking src/model_surface.py and src/covariates/*, which do not exist in the repo's src-layout package structure. That meant code changes to the live model surface or feature-selection logic could leave the cached BG prior silently stale unless a human remembered to force a rebuild. The fix was to point the dependency check at the real src/crimerisk/model_surface.py and src/crimerisk/covariates/* files.
next_action: When a cache invalidation rule depends on code files, make it watch the real live module paths, not an older repo layout or guessed placeholder paths.

current_rule: Invalidate the canonical city-share cache on builder-code changes as well as packet/config/raw-input changes.
evidence_summary: An architecture-audit pass found that src/crimerisk/city_shares.py only invalidated city_incident_share_surface.parquet when packet gates, central configs, or declared raw input files changed. If the actual share-building logic changed in src/crimerisk/city_shares.py or src/crimerisk/city_incidents.py, the cache could still be silently reused unless a human passed a force flag. The fix was to include those two live code files in the city-share dependency set.
next_action: When a cached artifact is built by repo code, include the builder modules themselves in the dependency contract so logic fixes do not leave stale artifacts live.

current_rule: Treat reviewed direct local annual publication rows as first-class source = local_publication_annual observations rather than packet-only municipal notes or SRS relabels.
evidence_summary: A follow-through source and wiring audit found that production-ready official annual extracts already existed in the municipal packet lane for cases such as Quincy, IL and Brunswick, GA, but the live build had no first-class local-publication source path. That left real direct local counts trapped in packet artifacts while zero-only SRS continuity rows still drove downstream estimation. The fix was to add a canonical local-publication loader in src/crimerisk/local_publications.py, promote production-ready packet extracts into explicit local_publication_annual observation rows, and carry that source through reporting-regime and municipal-estimation stages. After rebuild, the live reporting-regime artifact contains 28 local_publication_annual rows and Quincy/Brunswick now resolve in municipal_estimates_2024.parquet as preferred_source = local_publication_annual with annual_only_but_usable observed counts rather than fill.
next_action: Keep reviewed local publication support as an explicit first-class source identity with clear promotion gates. Do not smuggle those rows in as SRS or leave them as packet-only truth once they are production-ready.

current_rule: Make build-reference-layers consume canonical promoted inputs under state/reference/inputs instead of reading review queue parquet files directly as production state.
evidence_summary: An architecture audit found that the canonical reference-layer build still defaulted to state/review/queues/local_resolution/*.parquet, which made production appear to depend directly on mutable review queue outputs. The underlying reviewed local-resolution parquets are still the source of truth at this stage, but they should be promoted into an explicit production input surface before reference artifacts are built. The fix was to change the canonical defaults to state/reference/inputs/*, add an explicit promote-reference-inputs stage, and make build-reference-layers require that promoted surface instead of silently rereading the review queue.
next_action: Separate review execution state from production build inputs explicitly. If reviewed queue outputs are still the current source of truth, promote them into a canonical production input surface and require that surface in downstream builds instead of reading the review queue directory directly as if it were the final build contract.

current_rule: Guard canonical build stages with explicit file locks and dependency blockers so duplicate or conflicting writers fail fast instead of silently mixing artifacts.
evidence_summary: A live rebuild pass exposed exactly the failure mode the tracker had been warning about: stale duplicate build workers were still running outside the visible session set, including orphaned build-observations and build-outputs processes, and a second observation rebuild could start while the first writer was still active. That made the repo look partially rebuilt even when artifacts were being written by overlapping workers. The fix was to add src/crimerisk/stage_locks.py, wrap the canonical write_v2_* build stages in explicit stage locks, define a small dependency-blocker map for stages that should not start while upstream or downstream artifact consumers are active, and make the CLI return a clean one-line refusal instead of a traceback on lock contention.
next_action: Keep the stage blocker map aligned to the real artifact dependency graph. If a stage starts reading or writing new canonical surfaces, update the lock contract at the same time so build concurrency does not drift back into undefined behavior.

current_rule: When a build stage explicitly promotes canonical inputs, the promoted files must materialize with fresh mtimes so downstream dependency checks can see the promotion.
evidence_summary: An architecture audit found that the new canonical promotion surfaces for city incident inputs and reference inputs were being written with shutil.copy2(...), which preserves the source file mtimes. That let downstream dependency checks treat the promoted input surface as older than cached artifacts even immediately after an explicit promotion step. The concrete failure was city_incident_share_surface.parquet silently reusing a stale offense-gate surface that still contained blocked San Francisco murder/rape and Seattle aggravated assault after promote-city-incident-inputs had been run. The fix was to make promotion stages write files with fresh mtimes instead of preserving source metadata, so explicit promotion invalidates dependent caches naturally.
next_action: Treat explicit promotion as a fresh materialization event. Do not preserve source mtimes on canonical promoted inputs when downstream cache invalidation depends on file freshness.

current_rule: Use the HistGradientBoostingRegressor defaults learning_rate=0.03, max_depth=5, max_iter=500, min_samples_leaf=20, l2_regularization=1.0 for the canonical ags_core block-group prior.
evidence_summary: The strongest completed non-default HGB candidate in archive/modeling/2026-03-27-benchmark-sweeps/2026-03-27 was slow_hist: learning_rate=0.03, max_depth=5, max_iter=500, min_samples_leaf=20, l2_regularization=1.0. After promotion and canonical rebuild, the live jurisdiction benchmark in state/modeling/jurisdiction_model_benchmark_2024.json now reads cv_r2_log_rate_mean = 0.4758952281479364, cv_r2_rate_mean = 0.3512602065064351, cv_rmse_log_rate_mean = 0.8296214553636749, and train_r2_log_rate_mean = 0.874059057772829. The paired canonical city-share benchmark in state/modeling/city_share_benchmark_2024.json remains effectively flat to slightly better on the held-out city surface: weighted_total_variation_distance_mean = 0.3733335787429639, weighted_pearson_share_mean = 0.4282007824221325, and weighted_top_10pct_true_mass_in_model_top_10pct_mean = 0.27646496976894624.
next_action: Keep slow_hist as the canonical default and use the paired jurisdiction plus held-out city-share benchmarks as the baseline for future feature/model comparisons rather than reopening default selection blindly.

current_rule: Refresh canonical observations before municipal-estimate rebuilds whenever promoted publication or reference inputs change, so municipal target-year estimation cannot silently reuse stale jurisdiction observations.
evidence_summary: A follow-through architecture audit found that municipal_estimates_artifact_is_current correctly watched upstream observation dependencies, but the canonical municipal rebuild path could still consume a stale jurisdiction_year_observations.parquet because only the reporting-regime path was auto-refreshed. The concrete risk was promoted local-publication, state-publication, or reference changes altering observation truth without forcing the jurisdiction observations artifact to be rebuilt before municipal target-year estimation. The fix was to make write_v2_municipal_estimates(...) ensure the observations artifacts are current before rebuilding and to make controls request municipal refresh through the canonical writer instead of an ad hoc direct build path.
next_action: Keep municipal target-year estimation behind the canonical observations surface. If promoted publication or reference inputs move, refresh observations before any municipal rebuild that consumes jurisdiction_year_observations.parquet.

current_rule: Keep the canonical state_publication_annual input surface explicitly 2024-only until a real multi-year contract exists.
evidence_summary: A follow-through audit found that the CLI and writer surface for build-state-publication-inputs still accepted an arbitrary year argument even though the live state-publication implementation is intentionally 2024-scoped: FDLE and Mississippi TOPS loaders only materialize the 2024 canonical surface, and observations only consume state_publication_annual rows for 2024. Allowing other years to overwrite the canonical parquet would create silent wrong-year poisoning rather than a real multi-year lane. The fix was to make the writer and docs fail fast on non-2024 requests and state the 2024-only contract explicitly.
next_action: Do not expose a generic year write path for a canonical surface that is only defined for one year. Fail fast until the multi-year contract is designed and wired end to end.

current_rule: Top-level stages that rebuild prerequisite canonical artifacts must hold their own stage lock before entering dependency resolution, while nested prerequisite stages ignore only that single parent-stage blocker.
evidence_summary: A live rebuild audit exposed a real race in both controls and outputs. write_v2_controls(...) and write_v2_outputs(...) were resolving prerequisite stages before taking their own stage lock, so duplicate build-controls or build-outputs runs could both enter dependency resolution with no parent-stage lock on disk. The concrete failure showed up in build-outputs: two separate output workers collided before outputs.lock existed, one failed because geometry was already active, and the repo briefly had active output writers with no surviving outputs.lock. The fix was to move the parent stage lock to the top of write_v2_controls(...) and write_v2_outputs(...), then let only their nested prerequisite stage calls ignore that single parent blocker while keeping the rest of the blocker graph intact.
next_action: keep_parent_stage_locks_covering_dependency_resolution_for_top_level_pipeline_stages_and_only_relax_the_specific_parent_blocker_for_nested_internal_calls

current_rule: Make reporting -> municipal -> controls freshness see through observation and promoted-input dependencies instead of trusting only immediate intermediate parquet mtimes.
evidence_summary: A follow-through architecture audit found that reporting_regimes.py already knew how to rebuild observations when stale, but municipal_estimator.py and controls.py were still deciding artifact freshness mainly from direct intermediate parquet mtimes. That meant promoted local/state publication inputs or refreshed raw/reference inputs could leave downstream reporting/municipal/control artifacts behaviorally stale while still looking current at the top level. The fix was to define recursive dependency paths so reporting, municipal estimates, and controls all see through observation freshness and promoted-input changes rather than only the nearest parquet timestamps.
next_action: When a canonical artifact depends on another cached stage, freshness checks must see through the upstream dependency contract rather than assuming the intermediate parquet is semantically current.

current_rule: Keep observation freshness defined by one canonical helper set with one dependency list rather than parallel duplicate definitions in observations.py.
evidence_summary: A follow-through architecture audit found that src/crimerisk/observations.py carried two separate definitions each of get_v2_observation_paths(...), observation_dependency_paths(...), and observations_artifacts_are_current(...). Python kept only the later block at runtime, which silently dropped code/publication/provenance dependencies that the earlier block had included, while the earlier block had omitted the full CIUS source-tree dependency set that the later block added. The fix was to collapse the duplicate helpers into one canonical implementation that combines both sides of the contract: reference outputs, raw SRS/NIBRS inputs, canonical local/state publication inputs, live builder/provenance modules, and the discovered CIUS source files.
next_action: Do not duplicate freshness helpers inside a stage module. Keep one canonical observation cache contract and extend that single dependency list when new inputs or code paths become behavior-bearing.

current_rule: Invalidate the canonical city-share surface on all path-valued builder inputs rather than on a special-cased subset of raw_dir and bg_crosswalk paths.
evidence_summary: A follow-through architecture audit found that src/crimerisk/city_shares.py already watched packet gates, builder code, raw incident directories, and the BG crosswalk, but it still special-cased only a subset of the builder kwargs instead of treating the builder contract generically. That left a stale-cache hole for other path-fed inputs such as state BG zips and any future builder path parameters that were not also duplicated into required_paths. The fix was to make the city-share dependency collector treat every path-valued builder kwarg as a dependency, expanding directories to their contained files and keeping file paths directly.
next_action: When a canonical cached artifact is built from a builder contract, watch every path-valued builder input rather than maintaining a brittle allowlist of special kwargs.

current_rule: Keep stage-lock files as clean self-healing JSON state rather than leaving NUL-padded or stale-active payloads on disk.
evidence_summary: After stage locks were added, the first live rebuild pass showed two payload-hygiene bugs. First, truncating a lock file without rewinding the file offset caused rewritten JSON to land after a hole, leaving NUL-prefixed payloads on disk. Second, killing stray hidden workers released the OS flock but left lock files saying active=true, which made the visible lock surface lie about current build activity. The fix was to rewind before each payload write and to make unlocked lock-file checks self-heal stale active payloads and sanitize old padded payloads when they are discovered.
next_action: Treat the lock file as a readable state surface as well as an OS lock. If the payload is rewritten, keep it valid JSON at byte zero and recover stale-active files when the underlying lock is already gone.

current_rule: Keep published-NIBRS alias matching in one shared helper instead of duplicating the same matching contract across source_selection.py and controls.py.
evidence_summary: A follow-through architecture audit found that src/crimerisk/source_selection.py and src/crimerisk/controls.py each carried effectively identical copies of the published-NIBRS alias-matching logic: the same allowed-type map, the same agency alias frame construction, and the same one-to-one state/name/offense matching against FBI-NIBRS-Tables-2024. That was exactly the kind of layered duplication that could let one path drift after a future fix. The fix was to extract the shared logic into src/crimerisk/published_nibrs.py and make both layers consume that one helper.
next_action: If two production stages rely on the same published-NIBRS alias contract, keep that contract in one shared helper rather than mirroring the same matcher in parallel files.

current_rule: Refresh canonical reference layers from the observation stage whenever promoted reference inputs or reference-bearing configs make the cached reference outputs stale.
evidence_summary: A follow-through architecture audit found that write_v2_observations(...) was trusting preexisting agency_master, jurisdiction_master, and agency_to_jurisdiction_crosswalk outputs with no formal freshness contract. That meant a promoted reference-input change or override/config edit could leave observations looking current against stale reference artifacts unless someone manually remembered to run build-reference-layers first. The fix was to add an explicit reference-layer dependency contract in src/crimerisk/reference_layers.py and make write_v2_observations(...) go back through write_v2_reference_layers(...) when the canonical reference surface is stale.
next_action: Keep reference freshness explicit at the stage boundary. If observations consume canonical reference outputs, they must verify and refresh that reference surface rather than assuming a manual prior rebuild happened.

current_rule: Make geometry freshness validate per-state cache shards recursively instead of trusting only the top-level crosswalk parquet mtimes.
evidence_summary: A geometry audit found that block_to_jurisdiction_crosswalk.parquet and block_group_to_jurisdiction_crosswalk.parquet could be freshly rewritten from stale blocks_by_state/*.parquet shards and still look current, because the old geometry_artifacts_are_current(...) helper watched only top-level outputs plus jurisdiction_master and geometry.py. The fix was to define recursive geometry freshness: each state shard is now checked against jurisdiction/reference scope, state_control_comparison.parquet, and the state TIGER tabblock/place/cousub inputs it depends on, and the top-level geometry outputs are only considered current if those underlying shards are current too.
next_action: Do not let a fresh top-level artifact hide stale shard state. For cached staged geometry, currentness must recurse through the state shards and their raw/reference inputs.

current_rule: Invalidate the canonical city-share surface on raw city-source and geometry-crosswalk changes and block city-share rebuilds against concurrent reference/geometry writes.
evidence_summary: A follow-through architecture audit found that city_incident_share_surface.parquet was only watching packet/config files and a narrow required-path list, while the actual build also depended on raw city incident trees and the canonical block-group crosswalk. That allowed raw-source or geometry changes to leave the city-share surface silently stale. The same audit found that the city_incident_shares stage was only blocked against outputs, not against concurrent reference_layers or geometry work. The fix was to extend the dependency contract to the raw_dir file trees and bg_crosswalk_parquet inputs used by each city builder, switch the cache check onto the shared artifact_is_current(...) helper, and block the city_incident_shares stage against reference_layers and geometry as well as outputs.
next_action: Treat the city-share surface as a real derived stage with full raw-input and geometry dependencies. If the stage reads the BG crosswalk or raw city feeds, those inputs belong in both freshness and lock contracts.

current_rule: Include the live federal comparison/reference inputs in the controls freshness contract rather than treating them as untracked side reads.
evidence_summary: A follow-through architecture audit found that controls.py was reading the FBI CDE CSV, the parsed published-NIBRS table, and agency_master/source-selection logic while _controls_dependency_paths(...) only tracked the immediate local observation/reporting/municipal intermediates. That meant the controls surface could stay apparently current after one of those real federal/reference inputs changed. The fix was to add the CDE CSV, the parsed 2024 published-NIBRS parquet, agency_master.parquet, and source_selection.py to the controls dependency set.
next_action: If a stage reads a federal comparison surface or a source-arbitration module directly, freshness must track it explicitly. Do not leave behavior-bearing side reads outside the canonical dependency contract.

current_rule: Keep published-NIBRS corroboration in one shared predicate and pass canonical agency-preferred rows forward inside controls instead of rebuilding them in parallel helper paths.
evidence_summary: A follow-through architecture audit found that published-NIBRS alias matching had already been centralized, but the corroboration predicate itself was still being re-expressed separately in src/crimerisk/source_selection.py and src/crimerisk/controls.py, while controls.py also rebuilt the full agency-preferred panel twice in separate jurisdiction-summary helpers. That kept source doctrine harder to reason about than it needed to be and made another future drift bug too likely. The fix was to add build_published_nibrs_corroboration_mask(...) in src/crimerisk/published_nibrs.py, route both source_selection.py and controls.py through that shared predicate, and compute agency-preferred rows once in build_jurisdiction_controls(...) before passing them to the downstream aggregation helpers.
next_action: If a downstream stage needs the same source-corroboration question, reuse the shared predicate and pass canonical agency-preferred rows forward instead of rebuilding them and restating source doctrine locally.

current_rule: Keep the canonical residual-share benchmark on the same HGB capacity tier as the promoted BG prior instead of silently benchmarking a weaker scratch-default model.
evidence_summary: The first canonical city residual benchmark script was left with conservative scratch defaults (`hist_max_iter = 300`, `hist_min_samples_leaf = 50`) even after the live BG prior had already promoted the `slow_hist` HGB tier (`hist_max_iter = 500`, `hist_min_samples_leaf = 20`). That made the canonical residual benchmark harder to interpret because it was evaluating a different capacity tier than the promoted main model surface. The fix was to align the benchmark script defaults with the promoted BG-prior defaults and rerun the canonical residual-share benchmark artifact on that aligned configuration.
next_action: If a benchmark is meant to inform the promoted production model lane, keep its default model capacity aligned with the promoted baseline instead of silently leaving it on an older scratch tier.

current_rule: Inject experimental BG feature families into benchmark paths only through explicit scratch hooks that preserve canonical outputs and record feature provenance.
evidence_summary: The first bounded Overture Places experiment required trying a new BG feature family without hand-wiring it into the canonical model surface or risking silent overwrite of the live benchmark artifacts. Before this pass, city residual benchmarking required ad hoc local merges and the jurisdiction benchmark had no supported way to evaluate scratch BG feature parquets. The fix was to centralize merge_extra_bg_features(...) in src/crimerisk/model_surface.py, add explicit `--extra-bg-features-path` hooks to scripts/build/benchmark_city_residuals.py and scripts/build/benchmark_models.py, keep non-default runs off canonical outputs unless explicitly promoted, and record `feature_source = extra_bg_feature` in model metadata for injected columns.
next_action: Use explicit scratch BG feature hooks for staged feature-family evaluation. Do not wire new exogenous feature sources into the canonical model path until they clear the paired jurisdiction and city-share/residual benchmarks and their source-time contract is documented.
